list: The official 55 trophies: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze. Names, descriptions and grades as PlayStation publishes them.

sources.exophase: The official trophy list as published on Exophase — the source of every trophy's name, description and grade in this file.
sources.psnprofiles: The PSNProfiles trophy list — the source of PSN's progress counts wherever a number is given (42 Shooting Range challenges, 14 drone race locations, 18 meditation spots, 52 areas, 9 gangs, 8 garage properties, 9 activity types, 500 choices).
sources.own: Our own advice, built from the official description alone. The game launched on 2026-11-19, so any step that goes beyond the description is labelled as not yet checked in the game — no location or trick is claimed as verified where the description does not say it.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: There is no task behind this one: it unlocks when the other 54 trophies are yours. Treat it as the finish line — the roadmap's five stages are the route to it, and the last trophy to fall is usually the 100% completion gold, A Long Road.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing. It is the first mission the game gives you, so it is the first trophy most players will earn — no preparation, no way to miss it, just play the story from the start.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 1. The trophy lands as the chapter ends, so keep working through the story missions in order; side content can wait.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 2. Same deal as the other chapter trophies: finish the story block and it pops. Keep the missions coming in order.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 3. By this point the map is wide open and the side activities are calling, but the trophy itself only wants the story done — a good moment to start the long grinds (stunts, vehicles, races) between missions, since nothing here closes off.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 4. The last chapter trophy before the finale. Before you push into the final mission, clear anything that needs your story partner beside you — Hot Together and Retail Therapy are far easier while the story still pairs you up.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission. The only gold the story hands out, and it asks for nothing but the last mission itself. The description names no mission, so this guide will not guess one either — finish the story. Sweep the partner and choice trophies first, since the finale can close off story pairings.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete Breakfast Run. A completion trophy: the rating, the approach and the medals do not matter, just finish the mission.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist. Another completion-only trophy. Heists tend to offer preparation and approach choices, but the trophy asks for none of that — take the approach you like and finish the job.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete Child's Play. Finish the mission and it pops; no medal, no timer, no optional objective is named in the description.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete Headliners. Completion is the whole ask. A useful mission to practise Combat Focus in — Gunslinger will want it later — but the mission itself only needs finishing.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete VCIA Takedown at the Vice City airport. Finish the mission; the description ties it to no vehicle, route or time. Remember the airport for Catch Me If You Can — an unscheduled departure at the same place.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete Operation Savage Glory, the last of the named-mission trophies. The name promises a big set-piece, so go in stocked — but the trophy still only asks for completion.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Attain 100% completion for the second gold. This is the real final boss of the platinum: it only opens once the story is done and the big counts are finished. Do it last, in Stage 5, and trust the in-game completion screen to say what is missing — the counts in this guide (250 stunts, 100 vehicles, 52 areas) are the pieces that feed the total.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts. Jumps, airtime, near misses — whatever the game counts, it counts anywhere in Leonida, so start early and let the number grow while you do everything else. Ramps and fast drives between missions are the steady way in; save a dedicated session for the final stretch and watch the in-game counter.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once. PSN tracks 9 activity types, so sample one round of each — races, fishing, the shooting range, drone races, the arcade, bowling, meditation and the rest — and it pops. Do it early in Stage 2: each first try also opens the deeper trophy behind that activity.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges — PSN's count, and the hardest skill trophy on the list. Learn each challenge's weapon and target pattern, retry freely, and gold them one at a time rather than in a single sitting. Accuracy beats speed in most range challenges: slow down, aim, and treat each gold as its own small win.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location — 14 of them, per PSN. Each location is its own race, so a win somewhere already won does not help the next one. Fly a practice lap to learn the course, then race to win, one location at a time.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Different events, not the same race 20 times. Spread across the race types and keep track of which events you have already won. If one race is stubborn, switch to another event: breadth is what counts, and there are more than 20 races to choose from.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a named rival, so this is a set encounter rather than a grind — take the challenge when it is offered and do not put it off, because a rival challenge may not wait around. Learn the fishing controls in a free session first, then challenge Cal once you are confident. Flagged missable: the description names one person and one challenge, not a repeatable activity.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete an arcade game — any cabinet, any game, just play one to the end. The easiest trophy in the activity set: pick the shortest game on offer if you only want the trophy. It also counts as one of the activity types for Master of None.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete Andy's final mission. Andy is a side character with a mission strand of their own: follow their missions to the last one. Do the strand when it appears rather than leaving every side mission for the end — and finishing Andy also moves Strangers & Freaks forward.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's final mission. Kenton is another side character with a mission strand: work through their missions to the last one and the trophy pops. The name hints at a boat, so expect water in this strand, but the trophy only needs the final mission finished. It also counts toward the 8 stranger strands.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete Billy's final mission. Billy's strand is another side-character line: follow it to its last mission and the trophy pops. The name suggests riding alone — a bike or a solo run may feature — but the description asks only that you finish the mission. It also advances Strangers & Freaks.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida. Each finished strand counts once, so you need eight different strangers, not eight missions for one person. Explore the map, answer stranger prompts as they appear, and finish each strand when it opens; a half-finished strand earns nothing yet. This is the silver that rewards playing the whole map, not just the story.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's final mission. Randy is another side character with a mission strand: follow it to its last mission and the trophy pops. The name suggests supply runs — driving and delivery work — but the trophy only needs the final mission finished. It also counts as one of the 8 stranger strands.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete Tyrone's final mission. Tyrone is the last of the named side characters with a finale trophy: finish the strand's final mission and it pops. Five character finales (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) plus the stranger strands are the side-mission backbone — clear them as they appear and Strangers & Freaks takes care of itself.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot across Leonida — 18 spots, per PSN. Meditation spots are quiet places scattered over the map, so this is a travelling trophy: visit each spot and meditate there, ticking them off as you go. Pair it with The Goodtime State and Whip It Good, since all three reward covering the map, and use the in-game counter to find the spots still missing.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. A unique animal is a one-of-a-kind creature, so this is a single hunt, not a grind — take Bret's job when it appears and do not let the animal get away, because a unique animal may not come back. Go in prepared: track it patiently and take the shot when it is clean. Flagged missable: the description names one unique animal for one person.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets. Cards are hidden around Leonida, and a set is only complete when every card in it is found — a scavenger hunt with a checklist. Search thoroughly, use the in-game collection screen to see which cards each set is missing, and revisit areas rather than hoping to stumble on the last card. Three full sets is the goal; extra cards beyond that do not add to this trophy.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations — the game's photo-style collectible, as PSN tracks it. The biggest location grind on the list: 100 spots, one action each, spread across the whole map. Fold it into your exploration for The Goodtime State — every new area is a chance to WAiNK It — and keep count in the game so the last few locations are a deliberate sweep, not a blind search.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges — the game's own challenge list, covering feats across combat, driving, activities and exploration. A late-game cleanup trophy: by the time the story and the activity trophies are done, the counter will already be well on its way. Check the in-game challenge list, pick off the easy ones first, and leave the deliberate ones for a final session.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat. The partner is the catch: this only works while the story has your partner with you, so do it during a story stretch where you fight side by side, before the finale closes those pairings off. Build heat with a crime spree, then break line of sight, hide, and wait for the stars to clear while your partner is still with you. Flagged missable: it needs a partner present at a 4-star moment.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level. The level must stay on through all three robberies. Plan the route first: pick three shops close together, rob each quickly, and keep moving between them so the heat never drops. Like Hot Together it needs your partner beside you, so do it while the story still pairs you up. Flagged missable for the partner requirement and the unbroken wanted level.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles — drive or ride each one and it counts as discovered. A variety trophy, not a mileage one: a new model counts, the same model again does not. Work through traffic, parking lots and garages, and hop into anything you have not driven yet. Pair it with On the Spot and with exploring Leonida for The Goodtime State.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus — the game's slow-mo aiming mode. Wait for a fight with a crowd of enemies, trigger Combat Focus when several are in view, and chain the takedowns before it ends. Pick a busy mission or a shootout with plenty of cover and plenty of targets, and do not waste the focus on one or two enemies: five in a single use is the whole ask, and the attempt can be retried.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the Vice City airport — leave by a way the airport did not schedule. In plain terms: get a plane (or another aircraft) and take off without following the airport's rules, most likely by stealing one from the tarmac or runway. Expect heavy police attention the moment you do it, so go in fast, pick the first flyable aircraft and get airborne before the response closes in. Flagged missable: it names a single stunt at a single place.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description is a joke with a tank in it: Rhinos are the game's tanks, and this trophy is about dealing with one — most likely taking one on, or taking one over, while the heat is on. The exact act is not spelled out in the official description, so this guide does not invent one: when Rhinos appear at high wanted levels, engage one — destroy it or steal it — and the trophy should follow. Flagged missable: it depends on a tank encounter happening at the right moment, so try it whenever a Rhino shows up rather than waiting for a perfect setup.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — a clean, quiet robbery. Plan it like a stealth job: go in when the store is quiet, keep out of sight lines, take what you need and leave before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails, so leave and try again rather than fighting through it — the trophy can be retried as often as needed, which is why it is not flagged missable. Patience is the whole skill here.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape each time — five successful vault jobs, with the getaway counting as part of the job. Vaults are the big robberies, so expect alarms, police and a chase after each one: plan the escape before you go in, and do not linger. One vault at a time, five times, and the silver is yours. Start it in Stage 4 and finish it before the final cleanup.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape — the classic GTA robbery in miniature. Armored trucks travel the roads of Leonida, so find one on the move, stop it, take the cash and get away before the police close in. A fast car and a quiet stretch of road help, and the escape matters as much as the robbery: losing the wanted level after the hit is what completes the trophy.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — all 52 areas, as PSN tracks them. The map trophy: visit every named area of the state, from Vice City to the swamps and the coast. Drive the roads, take the side routes, and watch the area counter in the game to see what is left. Fold it into everything else: meditation spots, WAiNK It locations, vehicles and card hunting all take you to new areas, so by the time the other exploration trophies are done this one should be nearly finished too.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang — one hit per gang, 9 gangs as PSN tracks them. Gangs run their own rackets around Leonida, so find each gang's operation, rob it and move on to the next. Keep a note of which gangs you have already hit, since the trophy counts gangs, not robberies: hitting the same gang twice earns nothing. Spread the hits across the map and expect each gang's territory to fight back.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — the game's quiet moment on the sand. Head to Ocean Beach, find the bar or the spot with the view, order a cocktail and take it in. Nothing to fight and nothing to miss: it can be done at any time, so save it for a breather between the harder trophies. A good one to pair with a sunset drive down the beachfront.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — drive a car straight through the showroom glass, the way the old games taught us. Pick a showroom, get a car inside or line one up outside, and drive out through the window. If the first attempt does not trigger it, try another showroom or another angle: the trophy can be retried, and the description asks for the smash itself, not a particular showroom.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley — play a game of bowling there. The trophy names a specific alley, so go to Kolt & Associates, pick up a ball and bowl. It asks for the follow-through, so finish the game rather than walking out halfway. This also counts as one of the activity types for Master of None, and it is the natural partner to Ten Pin.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal. The description is deliberately vague, and this guide will not pretend to know the exact moment: it reads as a story beat where a partnership does something the public notices, most likely a mission or a choice involving both protagonists. Play the story, watch for partnership moments, and keep a save before big story choices so a missed beat can be replayed. Flagged missable: the description ties it to a single partnership moment rather than a repeatable act.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Choices made, for better or worse. PSN tracks a count up to 500. This trophy counts the choices you make across the whole game, from dialogue options to story decisions, so it grows naturally as you play and talk to people. Do not rush it: make choices whenever the game offers them, in missions and in the open world, and the count climbs. Flagged missable only in the soft sense — a playthrough that skips dialogue and avoids decisions will reach the finale short of the count, so choose often and keep a save before the biggest story choices.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm. Succeed at something on your second try after failing it once. The honest way to earn it is to fail something, then succeed at the same thing right after. Pick a low-stakes challenge you can fail safely (a race, a minigame, a mission objective), fail it once on purpose, then win it on the next attempt. Flagged missable: it needs a first failure followed by a success — a perfect first try everywhere leaves nothing to retry.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? The description is a question, and this guide will not invent the answer: it reads as a strange, one-off event somewhere in Leonida, the kind of weird encounter this series hides in the corners of the map. Explore odd places, follow strange prompts and keep your eyes open late at night; when something unexplainable happens, the trophy is the game's way of saying you found it. Flagged missable: a one-off event can be walked past and never repeated.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by — knock people down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle. Drive slowly past a group on foot, swing a melee weapon from the vehicle as you pass, and knock them down. A crowded pavement and a slow car are the setup; speed makes the swing miss, so crawl past and let the melee do the work. It pairs naturally with Let’s Go Bowling at the Kolt & Associates alley.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are dirty money from robberies and heists, and your contacts clean them for a cut — so this trophy grows out of the robbery trophies: the more vaults, trucks and gang operations you hit, the more marked money you have to launder. Keep laundering as you go rather than hoarding it, and the $250,000 total arrives during the endgame cleanup.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — weapons, clothes, cars, food, anything the shops of Leonida sell. This one takes care of itself if you buy gear as you play, but it is easy to finish short if you hoard cash: check the total in the game, and if you are close, spend the difference on something useful — ammo, a car, a wardrobe — rather than letting it sit. It pairs with Dime on the Dollar, since laundered money is money you can spend.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties — the count is PSN's. Garages are bought with in-game money, so this trophy is a spending goal as much as a property one: earn cash from missions and robberies, then buy each garage as it becomes available. Garages also store the vehicles you discover for Whip It Good and register for On the Spot, so buy them as you go rather than saving them all for the end.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The app is the in-game vehicle service: take vehicles you find to the Scooter Bros app and register them, one by one, until the count hits 10. Use the variety you are already discovering for Whip It Good — any 10 different vehicles will do — and register them as you find them rather than collecting a pile first.
